reason: Code Assist can answer 2xx with a non-JSON body. The catch turns that into a typed CodeAssistError that Pi shows at sign-in. Logging to stderr as well would write raw output into the Pi TUI.

googleErrorMessage runs on every failed request, and proxies often answer 502/429 with an HTML body. The catch must swallow that and return undefined so the caller falls back to the HTTP status text. Throwing would replace the real HTTP error and break retry handling; logging would flood the TUI.
A malformed SSE event becomes an Error that the stream reports as an `error` event. Logging to stderr as well would write raw output into the Pi TUI while the same failure is already shown.

The Pi stream contract is that streamCodeAssist never throws: every failure must end the stream with an `error` event so the agent loop can retry or report it. Rethrowing would leave the stream unterminated, and console.error would write into the Pi TUI.
AssistantMessageEventStream.push is the Pi host's own API for sending events to the agent loop. It is the only way to emit stream events, so it cannot be replaced with a copy.
